newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up after mixed pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up after mixed pre-holiday trade.

text.p: CME lumber futures ranged on both sides of previous levels for much of the pre-holiday shortened session and finished mostly higher on support from expected bottoming in cash, traders said.
Futures ended at 1200 CST/1800 GMT ahead of Thanksgiving Thursday and prices ended up $4.40 per tbf to off $3.50 with January up $3.50 at $382.20 and March up $0.20 at $370.50.

Although Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $378 per tbf, down $20 from last Friday and $47 under the week-ago quote, cash prices are seen firming. Cash spruce prices have tumbled $112 from the record high $480 hit earlier this month.
Expectations are that demand for lumber will improve after Thanksgiving before easing again later around Christmas. Bull spreading added to January's gains.

"There is an expectation out there among bullish traders that there is going to be a retail buy on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday of next week," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Lumber output also slows due to the holiday and wintery weather, which could underpin prices, cash sources added.
Lumber closed early at noon CST and will be closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving Day holiday.
